title: Circles
prerequisites: Chord and angle properties of circles from Class 9.
Idea of a line touching a curve.

topics.title: Tangent to a Circle and Its Properties
topics.quick_summary: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius at that point, and the two tangents from an external point are equal in length.
topics.real_life: A bicycle chain leaves each sprocket along a tangent, and the two straight stretches from a common point are always of equal length.

detailed.definition: A tangent to a circle is a line that intersects the circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact. A secant intersects the circle at two points.
detailed.key_idea: The tangent–radius perpendicularity is the key to every problem in this chapter. Drawing the radius to the point of contact immediately creates a right triangle to work with.
detailed.working_principle: From an external point P, the two tangent lengths PA and PB are equal because triangles OAP and OBP are congruent by RHS, sharing OP and having equal radii.
applications: No tangent can be drawn from a point inside the circle; exactly one from a point on it; exactly two from an external point.
The length of a tangent from an external point is √(d² − r²), where d is the distance from the centre.
OP bisects both the angle between the tangents and the angle at the centre.

points: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
Tangents drawn from an external point are equal in length.
A circle has infinitely many tangents, one at each point.
Tangent length from an external point = √(d² − r²).
The line joining the external point to the centre bisects the angle between the tangents.
mistakes: Assuming the tangent is perpendicular to the chord rather than to the radius.
Trying to draw a tangent from a point inside the circle.
Using the radius in place of the distance from the centre in the tangent-length formula.
topics.memory_hook: 'Radius meets tangent at a right angle' — draw that radius and a right triangle appears.
topics.advanced: A tangent is the limiting position of a secant as the two intersection points merge. This limiting idea is precisely what a derivative captures in calculus.

formulas.name: Length of a Tangent
formulas.variables: d = distance of the external point from the centre, r = radius of the circle.
formulas.when_to_use: To find the tangent length from a point outside the circle.
formulas.common_mistakes: Adding instead of subtracting under the root.
formulas.shortcut: It is just Pythagoras on the right triangle formed by radius, tangent and the line to the centre.
